materials.title: A Java class and the method that starts it
objectives: Name a class and one object of that class
Recognize the standard application entry method
State that this site does not compile or run Java
prerequisites: You can read a short code block and say what a file is named
materials.summary: A class is the blueprint. An object is one ticket built from it. A standard application starts at public static void main(String[] args). This site will not compile the file.

sources.label: Oracle tutorial: A Closer Look at the Hello World Application

examples: public class Ticket { } lives in Ticket.java
exercises: Write the class line and the main method signature only. Do not add a framework.

materials.title: Methods that return a title or refuse a blank one
objectives: Write a method that returns a cleaned title
Refuse a blank title instead of inventing one
Catch only the failure you named
materials.summary: Trim the title, then reject it when nothing remains. Compare text with equals, not ==. Catch IllegalArgumentException, not every Exception.
examples: if (title == null || title.trim().isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("title is blank");
exercises: Show one accepted call and one rejected call. Do not invent Untitled.

materials.title: A React component and the props a parent passes
objectives: Describe a component as a function that returns UI
State that this site will not render the component
prerequisites: You can read a function call and a returned value
materials.summary: A component function returns a description of UI. Props are inputs from the parent. The child reads them. This application does not render the JSX.

sources.label: React docs: Passing Props to a Component
React docs: Writing Markup with JSX

exercises: Name the prop and the parent value that fills it. Do not add a data fetch.

materials.title: State and a controlled title input
objectives: Wire an input so React holds the current title
Avoid reading the new title on the next line of the same handler
materials.summary: useState keeps the title between renders. A controlled input uses value and onChange. setTitle schedules the next render; the next line still sees the old title.

sources.label: React docs: State: A Component's Memory

examples: const [title, setTitle] = useState(''); <input value={title} onChange={(event) => setTitle(event.target.value)} />
exercises: Write the setter call for a blank title, then say what title still holds on the next line.

materials.title: Read one HTTP request and its status
objectives: Name method, path, and status on one exchange
Separate 201, 400, and 404 in the supplied log
Refuse a conclusion the status does not support
prerequisites: You can read a small table of rows
materials.summary: A request has a method and a path. The response has a status. In this log, 201 means created, 400 means the request was rejected, and 404 means that ticket was not found.
examples: POST /tickets 201 means the create request was accepted and a ticket was created.
exercises: From the project log, count 200 responses without treating 201 as 200.

materials.title: The page and the API are two programs
objectives: Separate what the page shows from what the API received
Explain one 400 and one 500 without swapping them
Say what this application will not execute
materials.summary: The page can show a title the API never received. A 400 is a rejected request. A 500 is a server failure. This app does not run either program.
examples: A heading that says Printer is not proof that POST /tickets received title Printer.
exercises: Name one field the page shows and one field the API received on the successful create.
